column1: # scripts/openapi-op-catalog.tsv — the ONE hand-written input of the published
# A row belongs here ONLY for an operation whose description cannot come from the
# code: an operation of the stable document (core/api/openapi.go builds those by hand,
# there is no handler seam to read), or a module route whose handler does not document
# itself in a form that can be published. scripts/openapi-op-descriptions names both
# cases, one line per operation, when it fails.
# This file does NOT decide which operations exist. A row for an operation that is not
# published is red; an operation with no row and no publishable doc comment is red; and
# a row for a module route whose handler HAS since been documented is red too, so one
# The right fix for a module route is usually not a row here: it is a doc comment on
# the handler, which then reaches this document for free and cannot drift from the code

Answers 200 while the process is alive. It is unauthenticated, exempt from the first-run setup gate, and exposes nothing beyond liveness.
Answers 200 while the process can serve. It runs no dependency check on purpose: a failing dependency must not trigger a liveness restart loop, which is what readiness is for.

Serves the Prometheus text exposition of structural engine counters and gauges: request rates, in-flight requests, ingest throughput, Go runtime and store reachability. It is unauthenticated and setup-exempt, and carries no tenant data, no credentials and no per-record detail.
Returns this document, the stable REST contract of the engine. It is served without authentication and before first-run setup so client code generation can fetch it from a fresh install.

Answers 200 when the process serves and the store is reachable, WITHOUT consulting leadership, so a hot standby is Ready to its orchestrator and a rolling update can progress. It answers 503 only when the store is down.

Answers 200 when the store is reachable AND this node is the active writer, so a load balancer drains a standby or a wedged instance. The store ping carries a short timeout, and a pending first-run setup is reported without failing readiness.
Returns the unauthenticated status summary: the same store and leader signals readiness probes use, enriched with the connector fleet aggregate when one is available. No tenant data is exposed.

Reads a page of the tenant evidence ledger. Paging is keyset by SEQUENCE, not a cursor, and the page runs FORWARDS from ?from in ascending sequence order — oldest first. The response carries head_seq, the chain tip, which is what a caller pairs with ?from to address the newest events.

Streams the tenant ledger in the requested format, carrying the chain-integrity fields so an external archive or SIEM holds an independently verifiable copy. The export is itself recorded in the ledger.
Returns the Ed25519 checkpoint verification key in PEM form, so an external party can verify exported checkpoints offline.
Reads the system-tenant evidence ledger, which records the cross-tenant operations. Superadmin only.
Verifies the ledger chain structurally and verifies every signed checkpoint against the engine key. The verification is not itself recorded, so it does not grow the chain it inspects.

Revokes the calling session. It applies to session principals only, never to an API token.
